exposure: Maternal factors (smoking, BMI, birth route, pregnancy weight gain, energy intake during lactation)
cohort: The study included 85 mothers and their babies.
finding: OPN concentrations in breast milk are influenced by maternal factors and are significantly correlated with infant growth parameters (weight, length, head circumference) and a reduction in fever-related infant hospitalizations.
mod_finding: Maternal birth route was identified as a factor associated with osteopontin levels in breast milk.
